title: Barriers and facilitators to the implementation of the national lung cancer screening program in Germany – an interprofessional mixed-methods study from the provider and patient perspective
summary: Since 2026, a new examination for the early detection of lung cancer has been available in Germany. People at increased risk can have their lungs checked using a special X-ray examination (computed tomography). For this program to work well, many processes between physicians and institutions must fit together. So far, little is known about what works well and where difficulties arise. In this study, we first talk with experts and patient representatives in interviews. We then survey further physicians as well as patients using questionnaires. In this way, we aim to find out which barriers exist and how early detection can be improved for everyone involved.
conditions: Special screening examination for neoplasm of respiratory organs

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Phase 1 (interviews): licensed physicians in pulmonology, general/family medicine, or occupational medicine with at least indirect involvement in lung cancer screening; and representatives of patient interests. Phase 2 (providers): licensed physicians in the above specialties. Phase 3 (patient level): screening-eligible persons or persons participating in lung cancer screening. For all: adulthood (≥ 18 years), sufficient German language skills, and written or (for the anonymous online surveys) implied informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of or limited capacity to consent; insufficient German language skills without the possibility of translation assistance (interview phase); refusal to participate.
